free_tier.stated: Promotional credit by code, not on signup: 'Use Code: FLY300VULTR ... Try Vultr for free with $300 free credit' and 'Use Code: 250VULTRFLY ... Try Vultr for free with $250 free credit'. The docs add 'Vultr offers free credits for up to 30 days for you to try our services.' New customers only.
free_tier.notes: the pricing page itself carries no credit; the amount needs a code entered at billing, and the 30-day term is in the docs rather than on the credit page

limits.value: USD 250 or USD 300 of promotional credit, up to 30 days, new customers only

limits_note: the credit is granted by code; without a code the account is paid-only

identity_cost.detail: card at signup, with a USD 0.00 verification deposit option; the provider may place a small temporary authorisation hold, amount not published; debit accepted; prepaid is not stated

notes: The credit is a promo code, so it is not a signup offer and it cannot be counted on until the code is applied. A payment method is required before any instance exists. Cloud Compute monthly prices are not stated to be capped at 672 hours, unlike VX1. Debit is documented and the verification deposit is USD 0.00, so no money is taken at signup. Prepaid is not addressed on either page read.

extras.price_note: a VPS bills by the month with an hourly rate capped at the monthly figure, so the two columns answer two questions: destroying the box between runs versus keeping it up.
extras.price_basis: 10 h/day column = 300 h at the hourly rate; 24/7 column = the monthly cap. Rates read's 2026-10-21 snapshot of the pricing page because the live fetch returned 403 on 2026-10-23.

payment_methods.hold_detail: no-deposit verification; provider may place a small temporary hold of unpublished size
payment_methods.identity: email and password, then a payment method for verification

binding_note: USD 250 over 30 days is 34.7 cents an hour; above that rate the balance ends before the month does
